facts.value: late 14th century. Name applied to Wyclif's followers in 1382

citations.excerpt: We first hear of it as referring to the Wycliffites in 1382, when the Cistercian Henry Crumpe applied the nickname to them in public at Oxford.
LOLLARDS, the name given to the English followers of John Wycliffe

facts.value: persisted in part until the English Reformation

citations.excerpt: they were the adherents of a religious movement which was widespread in the end of the 14th and beginning of the 15th centuries, and to some extent maintained itself on to the Reformation.

facts.value: An English movement following Wyclif. His disciple Nicolas Hereford helped translate the Bible into English.

citations.excerpt: Wycliffe left three intimate disciples:—Nicolas Hereford, a doctor of theology of Oxford, who had helped his master to translate the Bible into English

facts.value_before_verify: An English movement following Wyclif, whose close disciples helped translate the Bible into English.
